events.name: Cameroon War (UPC insurgency)

toll.text: The commander of French forces reported to his superiors that 20,000 people were killed in 1960 alone. One historian puts deaths in 1955-59 at around 10,000; another says several tens of thousands died, mostly after independence. A British embassy figure of 1964 gives 61,300 to 76,300 civilian deaths, about 80 percent in the Bamileke region. An opinion piece in Al Jazeera (2012) gives 100,000 to 400,000 for 1959-64 and 120,000 for 1960 alone, without a source; a historian of the war calls estimates of hundreds of thousands or a million not credible.
toll.note: Low is the French commander's figure for 1960 alone (a floor for the whole war); high is the highest published estimate, which is not documented.

events.says: Armed conflict between the French colonial administration, then the government of independent Cameroon with French forces, and the nationalist Union of the Peoples of Cameroon (UPC) and its allies, from 1955 until the mid-1960s, centred on the Bamileke region.
events.open: Neither the French administration nor the Cameroonian state kept an accurate count of the dead. Estimates cover different years (1955-59, 1959-64, 1960 alone) and cannot be added. Wikipedia lists 75,000 for the independence phase against another account giving about 10,000 for 1955-59. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: First Sudanese Civil War

toll.text: Estimates run from 250,000 (Correlates of War, 1963-72) and 500,000 (several reference works; 'hunger was the worst killer' per a 2001 Berkeley summary) to 700,000 (Bercovitch and Jackson, 1963-72) and 1 million (Wikipedia, citing a 2018 book). Wikipedia's infobox gives 500,000 to 1 million killed, including more than 100,000 combatants.
toll.note: Low is the Correlates of War figure for 1963-72; high is the highest figure cited. Most deaths were civilians, many from hunger.

events.says: War between the Sudanese government and southern Sudanese forces, from 1955 to 1972.
events.open: No count was made. The figure of one in five dead being combatants is a rough ratio quoted in Wikipedia. Some sources count only the years of the Anyanya movement after 1963. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: Vietnam War

toll.text: Hirschman and colleagues (1995) estimated 791,000 to 1,141,000 Vietnamese deaths for 1965-75 (most likely 882,000). Lewy gave 1,353,000 for North and South Vietnam (1965-74). The Vietnamese government (1995) gave 1.1 million North Vietnamese and Viet Cong fighters and 2 million civilians, 3.4 million including South Vietnamese and allied dead. A 2008 BMJ survey study estimated 3,812,000 violent war deaths in Vietnam for 1955-2002 (95 percent interval 2.2-5.9 million), of which 3,091,000 for 1955-75. US military deaths number 58,220 in the National Archives file (58,281 on the memorial wall in 2021).
toll.note: Low is the 1965-75 estimate for Vietnamese deaths; high is the survey estimate for 1955-2002. They count different years and groups; Laos and Cambodia deaths are separate.

events.says: War in Vietnam between the communist government of North Vietnam with the Viet Cong and the government of South Vietnam supported by the United States and allies, spreading to Laos and Cambodia, from 1955 to 1975.
events.open: Counts vary with the years included, whether civilians killed by both sides are counted, and whether deaths after 1975 are included. Wikidata holds two values (1,291,426 and 4,211,459). Estimates for South Vietnamese army dead range from 171,331 to 313,000.

events.name: Laotian Civil War

toll.text: Wikipedia gives 20,000 to 62,000 killed. A 2008 BMJ survey study estimated 62,000 violent war deaths in Laos for 1955-2002 (95 percent interval 28,000-115,000), against 20,000 in the Uppsala/PRIO database. Necrometrics lists 54,000 war dead (Rummel), and the Laotian government said in 2017 that explosive ordnance had caused 29,522 deaths during and since the war.
toll.note: Low is the Uppsala/PRIO battle-death figure; high is the survey central estimate. The survey interval reaches 115,000.

events.says: Civil war in Laos from 1959 to 1975 between the Kingdom of Laos, with Thailand and the United States, and the Pathet Lao, with North Vietnam, linked to the Vietnam War.
events.open: The 20,000-62,000 range has no stated method. Aerial bombing deaths are not counted separately in the sources read. The ordnance figure covers deaths during and after the war.

events.name: Congo Crisis

toll.text: Reference compilations put total deaths at about 100,000 (Smith, 1997; Correlates of War; Eckhardt), 100,000-110,000 (Bercovitch and Jackson) and at least 200,000 (a 1977 history of the Congo). A political-violence dataset counted 14,003 deaths for 1958-67. Wikipedia gives about 100,000 and, within it, around 3,000 Luba civilians killed in South Kasai.
toll.note: Low is the common reference figure; high is the 1977 history's 'at least 200,000'. The dataset's 14,003 counts only recorded political violence.

events.says: Period of political crisis and civil conflict after the Congo's independence from Belgium on 30 June 1960: a mutiny of the Force Publique, the secessions of Katanga and South Kasai, a UN operation (ONUC), a rebel insurgency and a second coup by Mobutu in November 1965.
events.open: No census of the dead exists. The counts mix fighting, massacres, famine and disease, and cover differing end dates (1964 or 1965). No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: Guatemalan Civil War

toll.text: The truth commission (CEH, 1999) documented 42,275 victims, including 23,671 arbitrary executions and 6,159 forced disappearances, and attributed 93 percent of the violations to the state and 3 percent to insurgents; 83 percent of victims were Maya. Wikipedia gives 40,000 to 200,000 killed or disappeared. Necrometrics lists 200,000 killed or disappeared (the commission, as reported), 100,000 dead plus 40,000 disappeared (press reports, 1996), and 140,000 dead. A 2008 BMJ survey estimated 20,000 violent war deaths (interval 10,000-34,000).
toll.note: Low is the number of victims the commission documented; high is the figure for all killed or disappeared given by press and reference works.

events.says: Armed conflict between Guatemalan governments, the army and allied paramilitaries and leftist insurgent groups, much of it in the Maya highlands, lasting from 1960 to 1996.
events.open: The 1981-83 period, counted by the commission as genocide against the Maya, has its own entry in this catalogue and overlaps this one; the deaths are not additional. The documented count is lower than the estimates because many victims were never reported. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: Portuguese Colonial War

toll.text: Necrometrics lists, for Angola, 55,000 (Eckhardt), 79,000 casualties (Hartman) and 120,000 (Dunnigan); for Mozambique, 30,000 (Eckhardt) and 63,500 (Hartman). Adding the lowest and the highest of these gives 85,000 and 183,500, without Guinea-Bissau. Wikipedia lists 8,831 Portuguese soldiers killed, an unlabelled block of 41,000-46,000 killed (probably on the insurgent side) and 70,000-110,000 civilians killed across the three territories.
toll.note: Low and high are sums of the lowest and highest Angola and Mozambique figures in the compilation; Guinea-Bissau is not included.

events.says: Anti-colonial wars fought by liberation movements against Portuguese forces in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau between 1961 and 1974.
events.open: The compilation figures partly count 'casualties', which may include wounded. Civilian numbers for Angola and Mozambique are given as wide ranges. Wikipedia flags the Mozambique and Guinea figures as possibly self-published. 7,447 Portuguese African troops are said to have been executed by PAIGC after the war. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: North Yemen civil war

toll.text: Necrometrics lists 70,000 (AP, 1991), 100,000 plus 1,000 Egyptians (Singer, Eckhardt) and 150,000 (1984 World Almanac). Wikipedia gives 100,000 to 200,000 killed overall, 15,194 to 26,000 Egyptians and 1,000 Saudis. A Washington Institute study says about 26,000 Egyptian soldiers died in Yemen.
toll.note: Low is the AP figure; high is Wikipedia's upper figure, which has no source I could read.

events.says: Civil war from 1962 to 1970 between republicans, supported by Egyptian forces, and royalists supported by Saudi Arabia.
events.open: No full count exists; royalist and republican losses are listed as unknown. Chemical warfare in the war is described on Wikipedia, with no death figures given. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: Papua conflict

toll.text: A 2005 University of Sydney study says at least 100,000 people have died under Indonesian control since 1963. Necrometrics lists 40,000 (30,000 in the 1962 conquest and 10,000 in the insurgency from 1965), 43,000, 150,000 'according to official figures' for 1963-83 (Le Monde Diplomatique, 2010) and more than 400,000 civilians alleged by human-rights groups (Newsweek, 2011). Wikipedia gives 100,000-300,000 civilians (a 2007 Pacific history) and 800,000 'Papuan claims'. A security task force reports 272 killed in its operations in 2021-25.
toll.note: Low is the earliest dated reference count; high is the highest claim cited. The figures cover different periods and none rests on a published count.

events.says: Long-running conflict between the Free Papua Movement and Indonesian security forces in the western half of New Guinea, since Indonesia took control of the territory in 1962-63.
events.open: Indonesia restricts foreign access, which limits independent counts. Some human-rights groups and academics call the violence genocide; this is disputed. Deaths from the 1960s-90s operations are poorly documented; recent counts of soldiers, police and civilians killed are far smaller. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.

events.name: Colombian armed conflict

toll.text: The National Centre for Historical Memory (2013) counted 220,000 dead for 1958-2013: 177,307 civilians and 40,787 fighters. The Truth Commission's final report (28 June 2022) counted 450,664 people killed for 1985-2018, about 80 percent civilians, and said that allowing for under-registration the true number could be around 800,000. The centre's observatory in 2026 reports 282,879 deaths in the armed conflict and its origins.
toll.note: Low is the 2013 centre count; high is the Truth Commission count, which covers a different period and uses more databases.

events.says: Armed conflict in Colombia among the state, left-wing guerrillas such as the FARC and ELN, and right-wing paramilitary groups, from the 1960s into the 2020s.
events.open: The start is dated 1958 or 1964. The Truth Commission attributes 45 percent of the killings to paramilitaries, 27 percent to guerrillas and 12 percent to state agents. The count of 121,768 people disappeared (1985-2016) is separate, and 7.7 million were displaced.

events.name: Cambodian Civil War

toll.text: Wikipedia gives 275,000 to 310,000 killed in the war, citing demographic studies. A chapter in the US National Research Council volume Forced Migration and Mortality (2001) puts the mortality impact of the 1970-75 war at about 300,000, and says later demographic reassessments (1993, 1995) put it at 300,000 or less. The same chapter notes an unsubstantiated 700,000 attributed to the Lon Nol period and a view that US bombing alone caused no more than 150,000 deaths.
toll.note: Low and high are the two ends of the Wikipedia range; the research chapter gives about 300,000.

events.says: Civil war between the Khmer Republic government, backed by the United States and South Vietnam, and the Khmer Rouge with North Vietnamese forces, from 1967 to 1975, with United States, South Vietnamese and North Vietnamese forces involved.
events.open: The effect of US bombing on civilian deaths is disputed (Wikipedia gives 30,000 to 150,000, including Khmer Rouge fighters). The deaths of the Khmer Rouge period that followed, 1975-79, are a separate and much larger toll.

events.name: Moro conflict

toll.text: Wikipedia lists about 30,000 killed (Philippine Army, 1970-96), with a claim of 50,000-60,000 and a rebel-side figure of 73,000 civilians for 1968-78. Necrometrics lists 50,000 (1990 SIPRI, Mindanao 1975-86), 60,000 (Bercovitch and Jackson, 1970-95), 75,000 (1969-97), 120,000 (a reference work, 1969-96) and 100,000-150,000 for Mindanao since 1971 (Ploughshares, 2000). A 2008 BMJ survey estimated 30,000 violent war deaths in the whole of the Philippines for 1955-2002.
toll.note: Low is the Philippine Army figure for 1970-96; high is the top of the 2000 Ploughshares estimate for Mindanao. Figures cover different years.

events.says: Armed struggle by Moro Muslim groups, among them the Moro National Liberation Front and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, against the Philippine state in Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, from the late 1960s.
events.open: Counts mix the Moro conflict with the communist insurgency in some sources. The 11,000 deaths for 1972-80 that Wikipedia lists are marked as contested. A conservative Uppsala count gives at least 6,015 killed in 1989-2012. Displacement exceeded 2 million. No archive of this war's dead by name was surveyed in this pass.
